sections.text:
2 Thessalonians follows up the first letter. The church is still suffering, and some have been shaken by a claim that the day of the Lord has already come. Paul says that certain things must happen first, including the appearing of a figure he calls the man of lawlessness.

He also addresses members who have stopped working and live off others, telling them to earn their own bread.
The letter presents itself as written by Paul with Silvanus and Timothy, soon after 1 Thessalonians. Some scholars think it was written later in Paul’s name, pointing to differences in tone.

Who or what the man of lawlessness is, and what holds him back, has been explained in many ways: a Roman emperor, a future individual, or a recurring pattern of opposition to God. Paul refers to teaching he gave in person, which we do not have, so caution is wise.
